construction: 26 parts in 1 step: a 4477 1×10 plate base, 1×3, 1×2 and 1×1 bricks stepping back each course, six 3040b 2×1 45° slopes on the leading edge, two 2449 inverted 75° 2×1×3 slopes and a 3665b inverted slope at the trailing edge, a 60477 4×1 18° slope at the root, a 61678 curved slope on top and trans-red 1×1 plates with a tile as the tail light.
interfaces: Stud directions: 26 parts, all up. The 1×10 plate's underside is the only interface; it sits on the fuselage spine studs.
lesson: A one-stud-thick swept fin: a brick stack whose leading edge steps back one 2×1 45° slope per course, a dark grey rudder strip of inverted 75° slopes at the trailing edge, a shallow 18° slope as the root fillet and a 4×1 curved slope as the tip cap, all on a 1×10 plate.
parent_context: `5892 - Airplane.ldr` places it at (90, −134, 0) with the identity matrix, on the rear fuselage centreline above the engines.
reuse_notes: Use it for any single fin: keep the stack one stud thick, step the leading edge with 45° slopes and the trailing edge with inverted 75° slopes, and change the courses to change the sweep. A two-stud fin needs 2×2 slopes instead.
